question: A 29-year-old man is brought to the emergency room 6 hours after the onset of severe epigastric pain and vomiting. His heart rate is 110/min and blood pressure is 98/72 mm Hg. He is diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, and fluid resuscitation with normal saline is initiated. Which of the following is the most likely immediate effect of fluid resuscitation in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Fluid resuscitation -> increase in circulating blood volume -> increase in venous return -> increase in cardiac preload -> increase in stroke volume -> increase in cardiac output -> increase in tissue perfusion -> 95%
analysis: Fluid resuscitation with normal saline in a patient with acute pancreatitis helps to improve intravascular volume and perfusion to vital organs. In this case, the most likely immediate effect of fluid resuscitation would be an increase in plasma oncotic pressure due to the infusion of normal saline, which contains proteins that help maintain plasma oncotic pressure.
